newsitem.title: DUBAI: EgyptAir takes Libyan pilgrims to Jeddah.
newsitem.headline: EgyptAir takes Libyan pilgrims to Jeddah.

text.p: The first EgyptAir flight carrying Libyans to Saudi Arabia for the annual Moslem haj pilgrimage in Mecca next month landed at Jeddah airport on Sunday, airline officials said.

"The Airbus A-300 plane carrying 253 passengers arrived in Jeddah shortly before midnight on Sunday and more will follow within the schedule, with six set for Monday alone," the official told Reuters by telephone from the kingdom.

EgyptAir said earlier this month it would fly 11,000 Libyans to Saudi Arabia on 45 flights from Libya's capital Tripoli and eastern port of Benghazi between March 30 and April 11. It flew an experimental flight to Jeddah on Saturday.
Libya is under a United Nations air embargo, but a U.N. Security Council commission has allowed EgyptAir to transport Libyans to Saudi Arabia.

The U.N. imposed flight sanctions on Libya in 1992 for failing to hand over two Libyan suspects for trial in the United States or Britain for the 1988 bombing of a Pan Am plane over Lockerbie, Scotland, that killed 270 people.
All flights must be non-stop between the authorised destinations and none of the planes used may be owned by or leased from Libya, which is not to gain financially from the flights.
Libya has occasionally violated the sanctions. The Libyan news agency JANA said on Saturday a Libyan Arab Airlines plane landed at Jeddah in defiance of the sanctions.
It said the flight was one of four planned departures from several Libyan airports to carry pilgrims to Saudi Arabia for the haj pilgrimage.
